name: Greg Murphy
page_title: Greg Murphy's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Republican for U.S. House (NC) - District 3

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "As a devout Christian and staunch believer of the unalienable right to life for all, Dr. Murphy is a proud supporter of pro-life issues. Dr. Murphy has had a lifelong allegiance to the unborn and the right-to-life."

"Today, #SCOTUS will hear oral arguments to determine the rights of states to implement restrictions on abortion. An unborn child is a human being, entitled to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. They must be protected under the law. #ProLife"
Rated 100% by National Right to Life Committee

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: "Part of the legislative process involves implementing policy, observing it in action, and adjusting it if it isn't working properly," said Murphy. "SNAP provides an essential service to low-income Americans. However, it's been abused by people who don't need it and the American taxpayer is footing the bill. I'm proud to introduce the SNAP Reform Act of 2021 to ensure that only those who actually need food stamps are the ones who receive them."
Rated 0% by NAtional Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare
Rated 3% by Alliance for Retired Americans
Voted against HR 1425 "Patient Protection and Affordable Care Enhancement Act."

"Dr. Murphy has spent his time in Congress fighting to simplify the tax code for working families and to lower the rates they have to pay, regardless of income. "Thanks to President Trump and House Republicans passing the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, the tax rates for hard working families are at historic lows. Yet thanks to out of control government spending, the fight for lower taxes for the American people must continue."

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "Although the concern over the high cost of prescription drugs is bipartisan, there is still much debate to be had about the best path moving forward. H.R. 3 is a well-intentioned but poorly executed plan to fix the often-unbearable price of prescription drugs in this country," said Murphy. "As a practicing urologist, I have seen more cures to diseases created in the last five years than the 70 preceding years combined. But by instituting price controls on prescription drugs, this legislation would significantly hamper research and development. There are better ways we can lower drug prices, like reigning in the practices of pharmacy benefit managers and curtailing direct-to-consumer advertising. It's imperative that we refrain from passing legislation that produces unintended consequences precluding scientists from finding the miraculous cures of tomorrow. We owe it to our children and grandchildren."

"As a practicing physician of over 30 years, the issue of healthcare and cost-effective relief is of utmost importance to Dr. Murphy. He has spent his career fighting the high-cost of prescription drugs and the lack of access to quality, on-time care for patients. As Vice Chairman of the Congressional Doctors Caucus, he will fight to make the healthcare system work for patients."

"Earlier this week, I was glad to join the North Carolina Biosciences Organization (@ncbio) for an important conversation about how we can lower prescription drug costs for patients while at the same time preserving American innovation for new cures."
"Instead of wasting more taxpayer time and money, we should be voting to fund our military, lower drug costs and finalize trade deals."
